text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Reducing inflation is a priority target for 1997, central bank governor Mugur Isarescu says in an interview.
ADEVARUL

- "We do not know how rough this winter is going to be, but we know the former executive did not put in place the reserves needed to get through the winter," president-elect Emil Constantinescu says in an interview.
- Democratic Convention deputy Sorin Dimitriu says the leu's rate, now held up through administrative measures, might fall to 9,500 to the dollar next February.
- The nuclear power plant at Cernavoda has not been connected to the national grid as it is still undergoing testing.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Romania has an export quota of 100,000 tonnes of scrap iron this year, which it will sell at $103 per tonne.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The central bank said it would back the package of economic measures suggested by the Dempocratic Convention and the Social Democratic Union.
- Romania launches a 50,000-leu banknote on Nov 20.
- Private ownership fund Transylvania has started distributing shareholders' certificates under the mass selloff.
- Renel RA electricity authority will get all the coal it needs this winter from lignite authority in Tirgu Jiu despite unpaid bills to its supplier.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA:
- President-elect Emil Constantinescu's victory is historical reparation after 50 years of communism.
- In Sunday's second round, 58 percent of workers voted for Constantinescu, IRSOP exit poll shows.
- Constantinescu got the majority of votes in the central region of Transylvania, western areas of Banat, Crisana and Maramures and on the Black Sea coast, in Dobrogea.
- A full-page report describes how thousands took to the streets on Sunday night in several cities across the country, to celebrate the opposition's victory.
- The Transylvanian city of Cluj is polluted by some 50 plants.
- Businessman and former tennis star Ion Tiriac said he would support the Democratic Convention's (CDR) "Contract with Romania", outlining measures for the first 200 days of government.
ADEVARUL
- Presidency spokesman Traian Chebeleu said he would return to his job in the foreign ministry.
- The newspaper prints a biography of Constantinescu who is 57 on Tuesday.
- The National Peasant Party (PNTCD), backbone of the CDR, should appoint a competent economist as prime minister, instead of a prominent party member, the newspaper says in editorial.
- The CDR hopes to appoint a prime minister and form a cabinet before end-November, Constantinescu said.
- Bucharest mayor Victor Ciorbea is among favourites for the position of prime minister, the newspaper says, quoting Mediafax news agency.
- French President Jacques Chirac sent a message to congratulate Constantinescu on his victory.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Constantinescu won the votes of Romania's most dynamic population, IRSOP surveys show.
- After the opposition's victory on Sunday, Romania is back on the front page of world newspapers.
- The newspaper prints biographies and interviews with PNTCD senator Radu Vasile and party vice-president Ulm Spineanu, likely candidates for the position of prime minister.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- NATO hails the Romanian election process as evidence of a solid democracy, the newspaper says, quoting Mediafax.
- Members of the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) will not be appointed local prefects for counties mainly inhabited by ethnic Hungarians, Radu Vasile said.
ZIUA
- November 17 was New Year's Eve for Romania's democracy.
- Dumitru Iuga, leader of Romanian state television trade union, demanded that the television's ruling board be changed completely.
- NATO Secretary General Javier Solana wants to meet Constantinescu, newspaper says, quoting Mediafax.
COTIDIANUL
- The CDR and UDMR are expected to start talks for a cooperation inside the government coalition.
- The PNTCD board is expected to decide on the new prime minister on Tuesday.
DIMINEATA
- President Ion Iliescu will become a member of the outgoing Party of Social Democracy.
- Defence Minister Gheorghe Tinca attends the meeting of Western European Union's defence ministers.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Most young people voted for Emil Constantinescu.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- Iliescu says he has fulfilled his mission as president in a difficult time for Romania. ($=3,502 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
